title: A Topical Reader of the Reformed Confessions
summary: The confessions of the Reformation, brought together by topic for reading and comparison.
description: The full text of 10 Reformed confessional documents, arranged topically, with every word from each confession appearing at least once. The confessions featured: Augsburg Confession, French Confession of Faith, Scots Confession, Belgic Confession, Heidelberg Catechism, Second Helvetic Confession, Thirty-Nine Articles, Canons of Dort, Westminster Confession of Faith, Westminster Larger Catechism.

title: Baptismal Regeneration of Elect Infants
author: Cornelius Burges
summary: Cornelius Burges on baptismal efficacy and the place of believers’ children in the Church.
description: First published in 1629, Baptismal Regeneration of Elect Infants by Cornelius Burges (1589-1665) gives a thorough defense of the efficacy of the sacrament of Baptism as it relates to the children of believers. Burges defends the thesis that elect infants ordinarily receive the Holy Spirit in Baptism, implanting in them the principal of spiritual life that, in God's own time, will bear fruit in faith and repentance. Drawing Extensively from Scripture, Church Fathers, Reformed Confessions, and the writings of eminent Reformed Divines such as Martin Bucer and Peter Martyr Vermigli, Burges presents a thoroughgoing defense of baptismal efficacy and the status of infants in Christ's Church.
contents: Elect infants and the gift of the Holy Spirit
Baptism in Scripture and the early Church
The testimony of the Reformed churches and divines

title: The Record of God and Duty of Faith Therein Required & The Antinomianism of the Marrow of Modern Divinity Detected
author: James Hadow
summary: Two works on saving faith, repentance, and the Marrow controversy by one of its leading opponents.
description: This volume brings together two important works of James Hadow (1667-1747), A Scottish Minister, Professor at St. Mary's College, and leading opponent of Marrow theology. The first, The Record of God and the Duty of Faith, is a sermon on 1 John 5:11-12 delivered by Hadow which examines the nature of saving faith and the Gospel's call to repent and believe in Christ. In the second, The Antinomianism of the Marrow of Modern Divinity, Hadow delivers a substantive and robust critique of E. Fisher's (1627) classic work; demonstrating that it is not freed from the charge of Antinomianism.
contents: The Record of God and Duty of Faith Therein Required (1719)
The Antinomianism of the Marrow of Modern Divinity Detected (1721)

title: The Cure of Melancholy and Overmuch Sorrow & God’s Goodness Vindicated
author: Richard Baxter
summary: Two pastoral works on excessive sorrow, spiritual comfort, and the goodness of God.
description: "In handling these, I shall observe this order: I. I shall show you when sorrow is overmuch. II. How overmuch sorrow doth swallow a man up. III. What are the causes of it. IV. What is the cure."
contents: The Cure of Melancholy and Overmuch Sorrow

title: A Key for Catholics
author: Richard Baxter
summary: Baxter’s extensive examination of Roman claims, church authority, and Christian unity.
description: First published in 1659, A Key for Catholics by Richard Baxter (1615-1691) is one of his most robust works against the Romanists. The work is comprised of two parts. In part one, Baxter presents a series of arguments against the claims of the church of Rome. Drawing from Scripture, the Church Fathers, and History, Baxter addresses questions and claims surrounding apostolic succession, papal supremacy, and the nature of the Church. In part two, Baxter focuses his attention on the unity of the Church. In particular, he demonstrates that ecclesiastical unity is not defined by allegiance to a particular ecclesiastical body, but Christ and Him alone.
contents: The claims of the Church of Rome
Scripture, tradition, and the authority of the Church
The unity of the catholic Church

title: The Certainty of Christianity without Popery, Naked Popery, and Roman Tradition Examined
author: Richard Baxter
summary: Three works defending the Protestant faith and examining Rome’s claims to authority and tradition.
description: “Published to direct the unskilful, how to defend their faith against Papists and Infidels, but especially against the Temptations of the Devil; that by saving their Faith, they may save their Holiness, their Comfort and their Souls." — The Certainty of Christianity without Popery
contents: The Certainty of Christianity without Popery
